title: The past and your weekend (Unit 5 final)
description: Unit 5 check after lessons 5 and 6, with the unit's final task.

items.instruction: Fill in the gap: What are you eating?
items.explanation: Review (Unit 4): essen changes e to i: du isst.

items.instruction: Fill in the gap: The film starts at eight.
Fill in the gap: Yesterday I slept for a long time.
items.explanation: schlafen takes haben: ich habe geschlafen.

items.instruction: Fill in the gap: On Sunday I stayed at home.
items.text: Am Sonntag ___ ich zu Hause geblieben.
items.explanation: bleiben takes sein: ich bin geblieben.

items.instruction: Fill in the gap: We ate fish.
Fill in the gap: I called my parents.
items.explanation: anrufen is separable: ge- goes in the middle: angerufen.

items.question: Which sentence means 'I went home'? (by train)
items.explanation: fahren takes sein (movement), and it's irregular: gefahren.

items.instruction: Fill in the gap: On Saturday I didn't have time.
items.explanation: haben in the past: ich hatte.

items.audio: Am Samstag war ich am See, und am Sonntag habe ich meine Eltern besucht.
items.question: What did the person do on Sunday?
items.explanation: am Sonntag habe ich meine Eltern besucht. besuchen has no ge-: besucht.

items.text: Das Wochenende war super, aber ich bin müde.

items.prompt: What did you do at the weekend?
answers: Was hast du am Wochenende gemacht
items.explanation: Question word, then hast, and the participle gemacht at the end.

items.instruction: Unit 5 final task, in two parts. Part 1: your colleague asks the first question below. Answer in 5-6 sentences: what you did on Saturday and on Sunday, and how it was (Perfekt, war, hatte). Part 2: in class, the teacher explains something much too fast and asks the second question. Answer in 2-3 sentences: ask them to repeat it more slowly and to explain one word (Könnten Sie ...?). Claude will check it. Then ask Claude for the live role-play: Claude plays the colleague, then the teacher.
items.prompt:
Kollegin: Guten Morgen! Wie war dein Wochenende?
Lehrer: ... Haben Sie das verstanden?
